We need to correlate. RX power drop ~7 dB (-11.7 to -18.8). TX unchanged. Commissioning loss 9.79 dB. Design attenuator 3 dB at B. So expected RX = TX - link loss - attenuator. TX ~1.3 dBm, link loss? At commissioning 9.79 dB A-ODF to B-ODF. Add 3 dB attenuator = 12.79 dB total. So expected RX ~ -11.5 dBm, matches pre-fault. Now RX -18.8 => extra ~7.3 dB loss.

OTDR from A shows loss 0.7 dB at 13.57 km. As-built element at 13.202 km is SC-04. That is close. 13.57 km is about 0.37 km beyond SC-04. Could be macrobend or bad splice. But 0.7 dB loss is not 7 dB.

OTDR from B shows no high loss. Event at 28.732 km loss -0.62 dB (negative). Hmm.

Maybe the fault is attenuator wrong value. Site notes: Receiver module replaced 2026-10-19 22:45, attenuator refitted from spares box. Design attenuator is 3 dB. Could have installed a 10 dB or 15 dB attenuator by mistake. That would increase loss by 7 dB (10-3=7). RX dropped ~7.1 dB. That matches.

Check OTDR: OTDR measures fibre only, not attenuator? Attenuator is at site B between ODF and receiver. OTDR from A sees reflective at 42.3 km (B-ODF) and end at 43.311 km. The distance from A to B-ODF is 41.16 km as per link record. OTDR shows 42.3 km to reflective (B-ODF). With 1 km launch/receive cords? Note says launch and receive cords of 1.000 km used; receive cord ends in open connector. So distance includes 1 km? Actually distances are fibre distances from ODF at shooting site. Launch cord 1 km? Hmm typical OTDR launch pulse includes 1 km cord. The note: Launch and receive cords of 1.000 km were used; the receive cord ends in an open connector. So the measured distance to far end includes launch cord? Typically OTDR measures from start of launch cord. The note might mean the trace shows extra 1 km. But the end is at 43.311 km from A. Subtract 1 km launch? 42.311 km to far end? Not matching.

Wait link length is 41.16 km. OTDR from A shows end at 43.311 km. That's about 2.15 km extra. Possibly due to fibre excess length: cable fibre excess length over cable 1.0 to 1.8 %. 41.16 km *1.8% ~0.74 km extra. Plus slack loops at splice closures. So plausible.

Attenuator is after B-ODF, so OTDR from A would see B-ODF reflective then attenuation? The attenuator is after ODF, so OTDR pulse goes into ODF connector, then attenuator, then receiver. Actually OTDR from A: the far end is the receiver's open? No the line is terminated at B receiver. The embedded OTDR is in line equipment at site A or B, testing the fibre plant. The OTDR from A would see the B-ODF connector as reflective, and the end of the fibre beyond? Maybe the patch cord to receiver continues? Hmm.

Better approach: If attenuator wrong, OTDR from A would still see fibre loss unchanged, because attenuator is after the fibre end (in the patch). The RX power drop is ~7 dB, TX stable, OTDR fibre loss unchanged (except 0.7 dB at 13.57 km). So likely the extra loss is not in fibre.

So fault is wrong attenuator at B-ATT. Design is 3 dB, but now probably 10 dB or 15 dB. Difference ~7 dB. If RX dropped from -11.7 to -18.8 = 7.1 dB. Attenuator change from 3 dB to 10 dB is 7 dB. That matches.

The main root cause: wrong attenuator installed after receiver replacement. So fault_type = wrong_attenuator, element_id = B-ATT, action = replace_attenuator.
